newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ISLANDERS REVERT TO FORMER OWNER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ISLANDERS REVERT TO FORMER OWNER.

text.p: The National Hockey League Friday returned the New York Islanders franchise to former owner John Pickett Friday after the sale to John Spano fell through.
Pickett will own the club until a new ownership group is found. But the future of the franchise on Long Island could be in jeopardy.
The arbitration hearing extending over parts of three days was chaired by NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman.

Pickett, who sold the team to Spano for $165 million including $80 million for its lucrative televison cable rights, asked for the return of the team when Spano did not meet a $17 million April payment deadline.
Spano, a Dallas businessman with New York roots, was introduced to Pickett by Bettman, and the Spano era has turned out to be an embarrassing error for all concerned.
Denis Potvin, the Islanders' former captain and Hall of Fame defenceman, revealed: "I was going to accept the position as president of the team, until Spano told me he was running out of money."
"Late last night John Spano and John Pickett reached an agreement under which John Spano will give up any conenction with the Islanders," said Bettman.

"Mr Pickett is going to be the owner. It is his intention to run this franchise as well as possible here in New York. It is also his intention to eventually sell the franchise, but he assures us it will remain on Long Island."

Pickett, who owned the team from 1978 through 1996 when Spano took over, has lived in Florida or Virginia much of the time. He has invested only a tiny portion of the television revenues in building the team back to the level it reached when it won four consecutive Stanley Cups from 1980-83.

New York Mets co-owners Nelson Doubleday and Fred Wilpon, who like the Islanders have a television contract with Cable Vision, have been reported as interested in buying the team. In addition, Bob Gutkowski, the former president of Madison Square Garden, and his Marquee Group have expressed interest.

Both the Mets group and Gutkowksi undoubtedly would keep the team on Long Island but would-be expansion cities such as Oklahoma City and Houston, who were rejected in the recent NHL expansion, might enter bids with the idea of moving the team.

Spano received an $80 million loan to purchase the team. Pickett is now working towards a further agreement between his group and the banks that had financed Spano's purchase. Pickett must reach an agreement with the banks by July 25 or the arbitration hearing will resume on July 28.
